top_choice_rationale: P002 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) credits the origination of nominal-rigidity mechanisms and their integration into a microfounded framework for monetary policy. This strand has not been recognised by an earlier prize. It is 25 to 45 years old, has been tested and modified through 2008 and 2021-23, and remains the common language of central-bank analysis. The three names map to separable contributions: Calvo's staggered pricing, Taylor's staggered contracts, and Woodford's synthesis. Micro evidence on state-dependent price adjustment qualifies the literal realism of time-dependent pricing. It does not remove Calvo's role as originator, and a citation should not present time-dependent pricing as an empirically settled description. The weaknesses are diffuse credit among eight names and Taylor's reliance on the contracts model, since the rule alone is thin. P001 (Melitz, Helpman) is a very close second, with cleaner attribution and more than twenty years of firm-level confirmation. I place P002 first on breadth and centrality, and P001 would be an entirely defensible outcome. P003 (Kiyotaki, Moore) is a clean mechanism but narrower and closer to the 2022 prize. I rank any of the three awards above no award. I do not treat support counts, or agreement with my co-author, as evidence of merit. I have not independently verified citation or priority details.
recusal_note: I co-authored the 2026 IJIO paper on menu costs with the chair (Hassler) and Ellingsen. That research is close to the nominal-rigidities literature behind P002, though none of the credited candidates (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) is a co-author. Hassler prefers the same trio, and I do not count that as independent evidence. My work on exchange-rate pass-through and invoicing currency is near P001's field, and my IO background is near B024, which is not on the slate. My spouse is a former prime minister, which is a public fact with no apparent bearing on any candidate. I am completing the ballot because the simulation does not adjudicate recusals.
